To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
environmental heating is an important risk factor for cardiovascular mortality among workers in the steel industry, which should be considered in the regulation of occupational health.

(1) the environmental heat load in the workplace is an occupational factor that can be a significant health hazard for workers; (2) the environmental heat exposure can be a risk factor for the development of cardiovascular and other diseases; (3) the environmental heat stress is associated with increased mortality from cardiovascular diseases; (4) the environmental heat can increase the risk of developing occupational diseases; (5) environmental heat exposure in the workplace can cause occupational diseases.
